card.name: Words leading into past-event wording
card.fires_on: Small words such as Previously, previously, who or not, right where a phrase about something that happened earlier is about to follow (a past status, discontinuation or earlier treatment).

modes.label: Previously in headings
modes.description: The word Previously starts a heading about conditions that were earlier held back by steroid treatment.
modes.example: Unmasking of Allergic Conditions<< Previously>> Suppressed by Systemic Corticoster

modes.label: Linking word before past status
modes.description: A word like who or previously sits between a patient group and a past event such as stopping a drug or being vaccinated.
modes.example: Consider benefits and risks before using ALYFTREK in patients<< who>> discontinued or interrupted elexacaftor

modes.label: Not after were
modes.description: The word not follows were in a clause about symptoms that were absent at the start.
modes.example: or were<< not>> part of the patient's presenting symptoms.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning recently or currently, such as recently, recent and lately.
card.plain: It marks the spot where the text is about to say something happened earlier or recently.
